extracted.intended_audience: users of the Singular computer-algebra system (researchers/developers) working with noncommutative algebras
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for the nctools.lib (and related) library routines in Singular: creating and manipulating noncommutative/special algebras (Weyl, Heisenberg, quantum matrices, super-commutative, etc.), computing related invariants and Groebner-basis-like constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gweights
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Gweights(r); r a ring or a square matrix. Return: intvec. Purpose: returns an integer weight vector whose weighting should be used to redefine the G-algebra to get the same non-commutative structure with respect to a weighted ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If input is a matrix and output is the zero vector then there is not a G-algebra structure associated to these relations with respect to the given variables. For a G-algebra one can instead use weightedRing to directly obtain an appropriate weighted ordering. Example shows Gweights(S) returning '2,1,1,1'.

rubrics_metrics.name: weightedRing
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: weightedRing(r); r a ring. Return: ring. Purpose: equip the variables of the given ring with weights so that the relations of the new ring (with weighted variables) satisfy the ordering condition for G-algebras (∀ i<j: lm w(d_{ij}) < w x_i x_j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activate the returned ring with setring. Example demonstrates weightedRing(S) producing weights and changing orderings; see also Gweights. The procedure emits the new 'weights' annotations and appropriate ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: ndcond
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ndcond(); Return: ideal. Purpose: compute the non-degeneracy conditions of the base ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If printlevel>0 the procedure displays intermediate (verbose) information. Example: calling ndcond() in a noncommutative algebra returns an ideal describing failed non-degeneracy conditions; verbose mode prints processing degree and failed relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weyl
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Weyl(). Return: ring. Purpose: create a Weyl algebra structure on the base ring (pairs of coordinates x_i and differentials d_i satisfying D(i)x(i)=x(i)D(i)+1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activate with setring. If the base ring has 2k variables they are treated as k coordinate/differential pairs by default. Optional non-zero argument treats odd variables as coordinates and even as differentials. Example shows D(i)x(i)=x(i)*D(i)+1 relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeWeyl
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: makeWeyl(n,[p]); n integer >0, p optional (field characteristic). Return: ring. Purpose: create the n-th Weyl algebra over Q or F_p; presentation uses D(i)x(i)=x(i)D(i)+1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activate the returned ring with setring. If p is not prime the next larger prime is used. Example: makeWeyl(3) yields Weyl algebra with relations D(i)x(i)=x(i)D(i)+1 for i=1..3.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeHeisenberg
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: makeHeisenberg(n, [p,d]); integer n (sets 2n+1 variables), optional p (field characteristic), optional d (power of h in the commutator). Return: ring. Purpose: create the n-th Heisenberg algebra over Q or F_p with relations y(j)x(i)=x(i)y(j)+h^d for i=j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activate with setring. If p is not prime the next larger prime is used. Example: makeHeisenberg(3,7,2) yields relations y(i)x(i)=x(i)y(i)+h^2; examples show variable orderings and how h^d appears.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exterior
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Exterior(); Return: qring. Purpose: create the exterior (anticommutative) algebra of a base ring: introduces relations x(j)x(i) = - x(i)x(j) for j>i and factors by the two-sided ideal generated by x(i)^2 for all i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activate with setring. Example shows anticommutation relations and quotient ideal listing x(i)^2. Useful to get standard exterior algebra behavior in Singular.

rubrics_metrics.name: findimAlgebra
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: findimAlgebra(M,[r]); M a matrix, r optional ring. Return: ring. Purpose: define a finite-dimensional algebra structure on a ring: the matrix M defines relations x(i)*x(j)=M[i,j] (by default in the base ring) and the procedure equips the ring with the noncommutative structure and exports an ideal fdQuot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure produces a factor algebra of a G-algebra modulo a two-sided ideal; relations split into G-algebra relations and the ideal to be factored out. Example: findimAlgebra(S) followed by twostd(fdQuot) yields a qring with listed quotient relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: superCommutative
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: superCommutative([b,[e,[Q]]]); Return: qring. Purpose: create a super-commutative algebra (GR-algebra) over a base ring introducing anticommutativity for variables in given block and quotienting by squares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default parameters: b=1, e=nvars(basering), Q=0. If b==e the resulting ring is commutative. The procedure creates relations var(j)var(i) = - var(i)var(j) for e>=j>i>=b and factors out x(b)^2,...,x(e)^2 (+Q). Example shows use with different b,e and optional ideal; printlevel>1 yields debug messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: rightStd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: rightStd(I); I an ideal/module. Return: same type as input. Purpose: compute a right Groebner basis of I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows computing rightStd(I) for a U(sl_2) example; options redSB and redTail may be relevant to behavior. Output is a right Groebner basis with possibly different sign/relations than left/std.

rubrics_metrics.name: rightNF
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: rightNF(v, M); v a poly/vector, M an ideal/module. Return: poly/vector. Purpose: compute a right normal form of v with respect to M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example contrasts left normal form NF(p,I) returning 0 but rightNF(p,I) returning 1; used in contexts where left/right normal forms differ in noncommutative settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: rightModulo
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: rightModulo(M,N); M,N ideals/modules. Return: module. Purpose: compute a right representation of the module (M+N)/N (assumes M,N are presentation matrices for right modules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates computing rightModulo(E,I), then making output canonical with rightStd and rightNF; used to compute right module quotients and representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: moduloSlim
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: moduloSlim(A,B); A,B module/matrix/ideal. Return: module. Purpose: compute modulo with slimgb as engine (slimgb algorithm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works both in commutative and noncommutative examples; examples show module outputs and matrix examples; one can post-process with std, NF, etc. Example includes a matrix/module case producing concrete element representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ncRelations
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ncRelations(r); r a ring. Return: list L with two matrices: L[1]=matrix of coefficients C, L[2]=matrix of polynomials D. Purpose: recover the noncommutative relations via matrices C and D from a noncommutative ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to export the internal representation of relations. Example: given explicit C and D matrices used to build nc_algebra, ncRelations(S) prints the same matrices back. See also G-algebras and ringlist references.

rubrics_metrics.name: isCentral
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isCentral(p); p poly. Return: int (1 if p commutes with all variables, 0 otherwise). Purpose: check whether p is central in a base ring (commutes with every generator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If printlevel>0 the procedure prints which variables fail commutation. Example: isCentral(c) returned 1 for central polynomial c, while isCentral(h) with printlevel=1 reported Non-central at: y, z and returned 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: isNC
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isNC(); Return: int (1 if base ring is noncommutative, 0 otherwise). Purpose: check whether a base ring is noncommutative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: isNC() returns 1 for a Weyl algebra, 0 for a purely polynomial ring. Use after setring to query current ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: isCommutative
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isCommutative(); Return: int (1 if base ring is commutative, 0 otherwise). Purpose: check whether base ring is commutative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: returns 1 for a commutative ring, 0 after setring to a Weyl algebra. Use to test ring properties programmatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: isWeyl
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isWeyl(); Return: int (1 if base ring is a Weyl algebra, 0 otherwise). Purpose: check whether base ring is a Weyl algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: isWeyl() returns 0 for a generic ring r, then 1 after creating Weyl(1) or constructing a nc_algebra with appropriate matrix M representing Weyl relations. Useful to confirm structure before calling Weyl-specific routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: UpOneMatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: UpOneMatrix(n); n integer. Return: intmat. Purpose: compute an n x n matrix with 1's in the whole upper triangle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helpful for setting noncommutative algebras with complicated coefficient matrices. Example: UpOneMatrix(3) printed an upper-triangular matrix and was used to form nc_algebra(C,0).

rubrics_metrics.name: AltVarStart
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: AltVarStart(); Return: int. Purpose: returns the number (index) of the first alternating variable of the base ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base ring should be a super-commutative algebra constructed by superCommutative; otherwise emits an error. Examples show alternating variable ranges printed via AltVarStart() and AltVarEnd().

rubrics_metrics.name: AltVarEnd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: AltVarEnd(); Return: int. Purpose: returns the number (index) of the last alternating variable of the base ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same notes as AltVarStart: requires a super-commutative algebra; examples demonstrate returned values and behavior in characteristic 2 where alternating range may collapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSCA
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: IsSCA(); Return: int. Purpose: returns 1 if base ring is a super-commutative algebra (SCA) and 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example uses IsSCA() to decide whether to print Alternating variables. Demonstrates constructing candidate SCA via nc_algebra with UpOneMatrix and testing; returns 1 for proper SCA created by superCommutative.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeModElimRing
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: makeModElimRing(L); L a list (usually contains a ring). Return: ring. Purpose: create a copy of a given ring equipped with the elimination ordering for module components (c,<).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical usage: pass a ring, get back a ring with component-elimination ordering suitable for module Groebner computations. Examples show effects on orderings and weight annotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: embedMat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: embedMat(A,m,n); A matrix, m,n integers. Return: matrix. Purpose: embed matrix A in the left upper corner of an m x n matrix (padding with zeros).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows embedding a 2x3 matrix into 3x4 producing zeros in bottom/right; useful to prepare blocks for larger matrix manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: perron
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: perron(L[,D]). Return: commutative ring with ideal 'Relations'. Purpose: compute polynomial relations ('Relations') between pairwise commuting polynomials of L (optionally up to given degree bound D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation inspired by Perron's theorem. Example computes relations for central elements in U(sl_2) modulo p and also works in commutative cases. The returned ring contains an exported Relations ideal; one can map Relations back to original ring to verify they vanish.

rubrics_metrics.name: quantMat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: quantMat(n[,p]); n integer (>1), p optional. Return: ring (quantum matrix algebra). Purpose: compute the quantum matrix ring of order n (O_q(M_n)); if p specified, q specialized to a p-th root of unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variables are listed row-wise (n*n variables). Activate returned ring with setring. Examples show commutation relations between y(i) variables for quantMat(2) and quantMat(2,5) (q specialized). Use with qminor for minors.

rubrics_metrics.name: qminor
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: qminor(I,J,n); I,J intvec, n int. Return: poly (quantum minor). Purpose: compute the quantum minor of a generic n*n quantum matrix. I and J are ordered lists of rows and columns (equal length).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base ring should be constructed using quantMat(n). Examples show qminor outputs for various index choices (2x2 and 3x3 minors) producing q-deformed determinant-like expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SymGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: SymGroup(n); n positive integer. Return: intmat. Purpose: represent the symmetric group S(n) via integer vectors (each row is a permutation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example prints the 6 permutations of S(3) as rows. Useful to iterate permutations, to feed into qminor/permutation-based constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: LengthSymElement
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: LengthSymElement(v); v intvec. Return: int. Purpose: determine the length (number of inversions) of the permutation given by v in some S(n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes v is a valid permutation representation; otherwise output may be meaningless. Example returns 9 for a length computation on a 10-element vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: LengthSym
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: LengthSym(M); M an intmat. Return: intvec. Purpose: determine a vector where the i-th element is the length of the permutation given by the i-th row of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes each row is a permutation in S(n). Example: LengthSym(SymGroup(3)) returns lengths [0,1,2,1,2,3]. See also LengthSymElement and SymGroup.
